english: Let $h_1,h_2,h_3,\dots$ be an infinite harmonic progression with $h_1=60$ and $h_5=12$. Then the number of terms of this progression that are integers is ______.
hindi: माना $h_1,h_2,h_3,\dots$ एक अनन्त हरात्मक श्रेढ़ी है जिसमें $h_1=60$ तथा $h_5=12$ है। तब इस श्रेढ़ी के उन पदों की संख्या, जो पूर्णांक हैं, ______ है।
solution: $h_n$ is an integer iff $n\mid60$; $60=2^2\cdot3\cdot5$ has $3\cdot2\cdot2=12$ divisors
solution_full: The reciprocals $\dfrac1{h_1},\dfrac1{h_2},\dots$ form an arithmetic progression; let its common difference be $D$.
Then $\dfrac1{h_n}=\dfrac1{60}+\dfrac{n-1}{60}=\dfrac{n}{60}$, so $h_n=\dfrac{60}{n}$ for every $n\ge1$ (all terms are defined since $\dfrac{n}{60}\neq0$).
$h_n=\dfrac{60}{n}$ is an integer exactly when $n$ divides $60$.
originality_note: New: an infinite HP is identified as h_n = 60/n from two terms, and the count of integer terms becomes a divisor count (way 5: HP linked with divisibility). Closest known: 'find the n-th term of the HP with given p-th and q-th terms'. Different because: the asked quantity is the number of integer terms of an infinite progression, which needs the divisor function.

concept_use.HP: The reciprocals form an AP with D = 1/60, so h_n = 60/n, and h_n is an integer iff n divides 60.
